evaluation: Agent review of the three-source research MVP
labels: Set before this run after inspecting the existing matcher and papers; not blinded, statistically representative, or founder-validated. Expected means a plausible research lead, not proof of the proposed application.

cases.idea: A local group that helps people build lasting friendships
cases.title: Help people reconnect after their first conversation
cases.criteria: People feel comfortable starting a conversation, giving a compliment, and talking about shared experiences. Success is a second meeting within two weeks.
cases.reason: The explicit example spans the three proposed applications.

cases.title: Newcomers assume nobody wants to see them again
cases.criteria: Help attendees recognize reciprocal interest after meeting for the first time.
cases.reason: Reciprocal-interest uncertainty is a plausible liking-gap lead, with transfer to attendance untested.

cases.title: People attend a group once but do not form connections that bring them back
cases.criteria: A second meeting within two weeks.
cases.reason: Original hypothetical need; generous exploratory relevance accepts all three previously proposed leads, not demonstrated retention effects.

cases.title: Do conversation partners underestimate how much others liked them?
cases.criteria: Compare how people judge an interaction with their partner's report.
cases.reason: Direct research question of the liking-gap paper.

cases.idea: A volunteer group welcoming new members
cases.title: Members hesitate to praise each other's contributions
cases.criteria: Make sincere appreciation feel less awkward.
cases.reason: Praise and appreciation are ordinary paraphrases of the compliment finding.

cases.idea: A volunteer group welcoming new members
cases.title: Would a compliment make the person receiving it feel awkward?
cases.criteria: Compare the sender's expected reaction with the recipient's reported reaction.

cases.title: Will a compliment help?
cases.reason: Singular wording of the appreciation need; paired with S08.

cases.title: Will compliments help?
cases.reason: Same need as S07 with plural wording; relevance should not depend on that inflection.

cases.title: Help members swap stories about shared activities
cases.criteria: Give newcomers an enjoyable icebreaker after a hike.
cases.reason: Exploratory adaptation of experience-related storytelling; the paper did not test this group intervention.

cases.idea: A discussion group about spending and experiences
cases.title: Do experiential purchases give people more happiness when talking about them?
cases.criteria: Understand the reported value of discussing experiences rather than possessions.
cases.reason: Direct subject of the purchase-storytelling study.

cases.title: Battery recycling
cases.reason: No relevant research in the current collection.

cases.title: Two people must review company invoices
cases.criteria: Prevent payment fraud with dual approval.
cases.reason: People, two and company refer to finance operations, not reciprocal liking.

cases.title: Five studies before deciding staffing budgets
cases.criteria: Compare cost forecasts and labor demand.
cases.reason: A study count supplies no topical connection to compliments.

cases.idea: A neighborhood club with travel barriers
cases.title: No compliment or conversation prompts
cases.criteria: People need transport, not talking activities, to attend.
cases.reason: The need explicitly rejects conversation interventions and asks about transport.

cases.title: Adjust meetup times around work and childcare
cases.reason: Social setting alone does not make these three papers relevant to scheduling.

cases.title: People need financial advice
cases.criteria: Help people choose company pensions and manage purchases.
cases.reason: Company and purchases occur in the papers but do not support pension or financial advice.
